report.program: Counseling, legal assistance, shelter and economic empowerment for survivors

acceptance.evidence: givebetter-nyc-sixth-seventh-independent-acceptance.json: primary-source checks, independent reconstruction of every scenario, and explicit uncertainty review; accepted as conditional alpha modeling, not measured causal impact.

report.priceScope: Illustrative marginal unrestricted gift; selected direct-service health pathways within whole-organization costs

what: Sanctuary provides counseling, legal assistance, shelter and economic support to survivors of gender violence.
Paid staff work alongside a substantial donated legal-service network.
Our very uncertain, conditional estimate is $34.6 million per 10 NYC-MSA QALYs for the quantified pathways within whole-recipient costs.
strengths: Integrated practical and clinical support addresses several barriers to safety.
An original audit separates paid costs from donated legal-service valuation.
A randomized psychological-advocacy trial supports the mental-health mechanism, with important transfer limits.
reservations: Service groups overlap and crisis clients are not all therapy completers.
The next gift's capacity and injury prevention effects are unmeasured.
Financial presentations differ and three comparable original years are not verified.

sections.what: Sanctuary for Families, Inc., EIN 13-3193119, provides survivor counseling, legal assistance, shelter and economic empowerment. We include New Beginnings Housing Development Fund Corporation because the audited portfolio is consolidated. The gift is unrestricted. [Services](https://sanctuaryforfamilies.org/impact/)
sections.monitoring: The primary-source audit records 9,230 total clients, over 2,600 clinical/crisis clients, over 7,000 legal clients and 428 shelter clients. Do not sum these overlapping groups. We use 2,600 as a lower-bound contact anchor and 428 for physical injury prevention. A 0.1 clinical-response fraction includes crisis-only contact, completion and improvement beyond existing care. Needed: all entrants, exposure, missing follow-up, validated health scores, physical injuries and cross-program IDs. [Evaluation](https://sanctuaryforfamilies.org/impact/evaluation/)
sections.qualitative: PATH randomized usual domestic-violence advocacy versus advocacy plus eight psychological sessions plus two follow-up sessions and found improved depression/distress at twelve months, with 64% follow-up. UK women aged 16 and older are not Sanctuary's entire mixed clinical/crisis cohort. This supports the mechanism, not our 0.08 utility or 0.1 net-response prior. Advocacy, legal success and safety are not automatically QALYs. [Original trial](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0205485)
sections.cost: The central conditional estimate is $34.6 million per 10 NYC-MSA QALYs (0.00028865 QALYs per $1,000). The $1,000 gift is scaled against $33,936,024 whole-recipient non-donated accrual cost. b=.5 assumes half historical output-per-dollar becomes marginal capacity. Counseling: 2,600 × 0.1 additional response × 0.08 utility × one finite year. Shelter injury: 428 × 0.03 absolute one-year risk reduction × 0.15 physical utility loss × 0.25-year episode × 0.75 overlap residual. Injury timing is uniform over one year, integrating the full episode through a 1.25-year horizon; no blanket half-duration factor. Clinical benefit starts after 0.25 years; annual mortality 0.005 and discount 0.03 are assumptions. No lives saved or lifetime benefits. Other legal/housing/income health effects are provisionally net zero, not a lower bound.
sections.funding: FY25 audited operating expense $102,237,655 + $387,934 event benefits = $102,625,589 gross; minus $68,528,009 donated legal services and $161,556 goods = $33,936,024 non-donated accrual cost, not cash spending. FY24 comparable is $31,917,251. All programs/support stay in scope. FY25 original return reports $33,654,637: Schedule D reconciles $102,237,655 - $68,528,009 - $55,009. Tax/event/noncash treatment explains why this is not our denominator; annual-report $33,539,090 remains unreconciled. Older original-return downloads failed. Only two comparable audited years are listed and no three-year mean is invented. Current public and volunteer support remain baseline; a marginal staffing or recruitment bottleneck is not established. [Audit](https://sanctuaryforfamilies.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Sanctuary-for-Families-FY25-Audit.pdf) [Original return](https://sanctuaryforfamilies.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Sanctuary-for-Families-990-FY25.pdf)

model.costScope: $1000 unrestricted gift scaled by all-recipient non-donated accrual cost including all support/event costs; current donated legal labor is baseline. Not social cost-effectiveness.
model.geographicAttribution: g=.95 prior for service beneficiaries within NYC MSA, not measured residence allocation. National precedent benefits unpriced; sensitivity .5–1.
model.formula: For pathway j: k=ln(1+d)-ln(1-m_j); F_j=exp(-k*lag_j)*(1-exp(-k*T_j))/k (T if k=0). Qall=(D/C)*b*sum(N_j*r_j*u_j*F_j*o_j)-h; Qedition=(D/C)*b*sum(N_j*r_j*u_j*F_j*o_j*g_j)-h*gH. Price10=10*D/Qedition if positive. For uniformly timed injury events over W years multiply F by (1-exp(-k*W))/(k*W). The full episode T follows each event, so horizon is lag+W+T.
model.counterfactual: Public survivor services, existing clinicians and pro-bono support continue. r counts extra response or absolute injury probability reduction. No full volunteer network credit.
model.attribution: b=.5 marginal output elasticity is a prior. Physical injury excludes mental-health sequelae and uses .75 residual-overlap factor. No restricted clinical allocation assumed.
model.uncertainty: Very weak. Clinical transfer, gift additionality and injury effects dominate. Zero or negative net health remains plausible.
model.nativeOutcomes: Additional clinical responders and physical injury episodes prevented; not summed service contacts or legal wins.

inputLegend.N: Observed service count when sourced; ICC modeled exposed population is judgment.

inputLegend.u: Annual incremental health utility conditional on causal success, all judgment.
inputLegend.T: Finite health duration in years; no lifelong extrapolation.
inputLegend.m: Annual mortality probability, assumed; survival affects duration only.
inputLegend.o: Residual overlap factor; ICC coalition attribution instead.
inputLegend.W: Injury risk window; event times uniform and entire episode counted after each event.
